decisions.reason: A directly addresses B as 'Jack' in turn 1, which is an explicit vocative establishing B's name.
'B is named Jack' and 'B's name is Jack' are bidirectionally equivalent statements about the same property (B's name), supported by the same evidence.

decisions.claim: B has something (likely a pet) that is also a lot of trouble
decisions.reason: The phrase 'just as much trouble' is a comparative that presupposes some referent is 'a lot of trouble,' but it does not necessarily establish that B has such a thing. A could be comparing to another of A's own pets, a general reference, or something else entirely. The claim that B specifically has something that is 'a lot of trouble' is an unsupported inference.
decisions.counterexample: B could reply: 'Haha, yeah, my puppy is also a handful!' or alternatively 'I don't have a pet at all' — the comparative in A's turn doesn't force B to be the owner of the compared item.
